people.elimelech.relations: Husband of Naomi. Father of Mahlon and Chilion.
people.elimelech.meaning: He leaves Bethlehem in a famine and takes his family to Moab. He dies there. In chapter 4 Boaz buys the land that was his.
people.naomi.relations: Wife of Elimelech. Mother of Mahlon and Chilion. Mother-in-law of Ruth and Orpah.
people.naomi.meaning: She loses her husband and both sons in Moab. She returns to Bethlehem and calls herself Mara, meaning bitter. She sends Ruth to Boaz at the threshing floor. At the end she nurses Ruth’s son Obed.
people.mahlon.relations: Son of Elimelech and Naomi. Brother of Chilion. Ruth 4:10 names Ruth as his wife.
people.mahlon.meaning: He moves to Moab with his parents and marries there. He dies with no child named. Boaz later marries Ruth to keep Mahlon’s name on his land.
people.chilion.relations: Son of Elimelech and Naomi. Brother of Mahlon.
people.chilion.meaning: He moves to Moab with his parents and marries there. He dies with no child named. Ruth was Mahlon’s wife, so Chilion’s wife was Orpah. In chapter 4 Boaz buys what was his.
people.ruth.meaning: She stays with Naomi and goes with her to Bethlehem. She picks up leftover grain in Boaz’s field to feed them both. At the threshing floor she asks Boaz to act as her near relative. She marries him and bears Obed.
people.orpah.relations: Daughter-in-law of Naomi. Sister-in-law of Ruth.
people.orpah.meaning: She sets out for Judah with Naomi and Ruth. Naomi tells her twice to go back. She weeps, kisses Naomi, and returns to her people in Moab.
people.boaz.role: Relative of Elimelech who marries Ruth
people.boaz.meaning: He lets Ruth gather grain in his field and keeps her safe. At the threshing floor he promises to help her. At the gate he buys Elimelech’s land before ten elders. He marries Ruth, and Obed is born.
people.harvest-supervisor.role: Unnamed servant set over Boaz’s reapers
people.harvest-supervisor.relations: Servant of Boaz. He answers Boaz’s question about Ruth.
people.harvest-supervisor.meaning: Boaz asks him who the young woman is. He says she is the Moabite who came back with Naomi. He says she asked to gather grain and has worked since morning.
people.nearer-redeemer.role: Unnamed closer relative who gives up his right
people.nearer-redeemer.meaning: Boaz stops him at the gate and offers him Elimelech’s land. He says he will buy it back. Boaz says the duty also includes Ruth. He gives up his right and takes off his sandal.
people.obed.relations: Son of Boaz and Ruth. Father of Jesse and grandfather of David.
people.obed.meaning: He is born after Boaz marries Ruth. Naomi takes him and nurses him. The neighbor women name him Obed.
people.jesse.relations: Son of Obed. Father of David.
people.jesse.meaning: Jesse does nothing in this book. Ruth 4:17 and 4:22 name him as Obed’s son and David’s father.
people.david.relations: Son of Jesse. Grandson of Obed.
people.david.meaning: David does nothing in this book. His name ends the family list in Ruth 4:22. The list runs from Perez through Boaz and Obed to him.
people.perez.meaning: The people at the gate ask that Boaz’s house be like Perez’s house. The closing family list starts with Perez. It names him as Hezron’s father.
people.hezron.relations: Son of Perez. Father of Ram.
people.hezron.meaning: Hezron does nothing in this book. The closing list names him as Perez’s son and Ram’s father.
people.ram.relations: Son of Hezron. Father of Amminadab.
people.ram.meaning: Ram does nothing in this book. The closing list names him as Hezron’s son and Amminadab’s father.
people.amminadab.meaning: Amminadab does nothing in this book. The closing list names him as Ram’s son and Nahshon’s father.
people.salmon.relations: Son of Nahshon. Father of Boaz.
people.salmon.meaning: Salmon does nothing in this book. The closing list names him as Nahshon’s son and Boaz’s father.
people.nahshon.relations: Son of Amminadab. Father of Salmon.
people.nahshon.meaning: Nahshon does nothing in this book. The closing list names him as Amminadab’s son and Salmon’s father.
people.leah.meaning: Leah does not act in this book. The people at the gate name her when they bless Ruth. They say Rachel and Leah built the house of Israel.
people.rachel.meaning: Rachel does not act in this book. The people at the gate ask the LORD to make Ruth like her and Leah. They say both women built the house of Israel.
people.judah.meaning: Judah does not act in this book. The people at the gate name him in their blessing. They say Tamar bore Perez to Judah.
people.tamar.role: Mother of Perez, named in the gate blessing
people.tamar.meaning: Tamar does not act in this book. The people at the gate say she bore Perez to Judah. They ask that Boaz’s house be like the house of Perez.
places.moab.summary: Elimelech takes his family here in a famine in chapter 1. He and both sons die here. Naomi and Ruth then leave for Bethlehem.
places.moab.limits: The marker shows the region only. The text does not say where the family lived.
places.bethlehem.summary: Elimelech’s family leaves this town in chapter 1, and Naomi returns with Ruth. Ruth gathers grain in Boaz’s field in chapter 2. Boaz settles the matter at the town gate in chapter 4.
places.bethlehem.limits: The marker shows the town’s general location. No one knows where Boaz’s field, threshing floor, or gate stood.
sources.web.limits: The text supplies the events and the family list. It cannot confirm event years or how people looked.
sources.atlas-canaan.limits: Coordinates are display estimates. A town marker does not confirm an event at that town.
sources.terrain.limits: Modern terrain is a map aid. It does not show ancient shorelines or towns.
sources.yale-ruth.summary: The study examines the two women’s bond, household survival, and devotion. It also covers doubt about the threshing-floor meeting.
sources.yale-ruth.limits: The published study guide was reviewed, not its video. Its final paragraph wrongly contrasts Ruth with Boaz in the family list. Ruth 4:18–22 names Boaz. This guide follows the biblical text.
sources.dm-ruth.summary: McClellan discusses Hebrew grammar in Ruth 2. He also compares the Hebrew and Greek readings. He notes the uncertain wording of verse 7.
sources.dm-ruth.limits: This is one scholar’s 2010 translation and notes. This guide keeps the World English Bible reading. His proposed readings are not treated as settled.
sources.lds-ruth.limits: The Ruth sections of the 1980 manual were reviewed. Its history claims are kept apart from independent evidence. Boaz is a relative, not Mahlon’s stated brother.
sources.cfm-2026-23.limits: This is Church teaching and application. It does not supply archaeological evidence or event dates.
sources.wiki-ruth.summary: Ruth follows a Moabite widow’s return with Naomi to Bethlehem. The household account ends with a family list connected to David.
sources.wiki-ruth.limits: Anyone can edit this source. Use it for background and to find other sources. Its disputed history claims need separate scholarly review.
chapters.*.mapNote: The points show Bethlehem and the region of Moab. The Moab point marks a region, not a town.
chapters.*.routeEvidence: The line joins Moab and Bethlehem, the two ends the text names. The real path around the Dead Sea is unknown.
